newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Canadian company signs gold mining deal with Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Canadian company signs gold mining deal with Zaire.

text.p: Zaire and Canadian company Banro Resources Corp have signed a gold and tin mining convention covering concessions in the east of the Central African country, Zairean state radio reported on Saturday.
The convention covers North and South Kivu and Maniema provinces, which are partly under the control of Tutsi-led rebels.

"Under the terms of this convention Banro Resources Corporation undertakes to invest $340 million in exploitation of gold and cassiterite (native tin dioxide) deposits in North Kivu, South Kivu and Maniema," the radio said.
It did not make clear when the deal was signed.
In the provinces in question, gold is mainly mined by the Kivu Mining and Industrial Company SIMINKI, in which Banro has a majority stake.
The radio said Banro would spread its investments over 20 years. The investments were expected to boost Zaire's gold production from 550 kilos (1,100 pounds) a year to 15 tonnes a year, it added.
